class_id: an ordering decision compares a time stamped by one machine's clock with a time stamped by another's; any drift between them misorders events that fall within the drift
feature: every before/after decision between an admin write and a database-stamped event: §9.2 item 9 (a document first seen after the admin save), item 27 (relaunch admin-clear), the status ladder guard (field_sources.updated_at), and any column written sometimes from the app host's clock and sometimes from the database's
symptom: one side of a comparison is stamped by the application host (new Date() in Node) and the other by the database (now() / defaultNow()). The two clocks drift independently (measured 2026-09-29: app host vs database about 0.3 s, uncontrolled). An event that happened after the other by less than the drift is read as before it, or the reverse; the error is silent, intermittent (the integration case failed 2 of 3 runs), and grows with any clock step on either host. The same defect appears inside ONE column when its INSERT path stamps from the app and its UPDATE path from the database.
first_seen: F-210, 2026-09-29. writeAdminFieldValue stamped field_sources.updated_at / field_protection_metadata.manually_edited_at from new Date() (admin-field-write.ts:696, main 7ae8c3cf) while documents.created_at is the database default; with the app clock 5 min behind, item 9 suggested a document first seen BEFORE the save (2 suggestions instead of 1); 5 min ahead, it missed the one first seen AFTER (0 instead of 1). field-sources-repository.ts INSERT used new Date(), its UPDATE now().
fix_prs: branch fix/admin-write-db-clock: admin writes read the database clock once per transaction (readDatabaseNow in packages/shared/src/db/database-clock.ts) or stamp sql now(); the field_sources INSERT stamps now() like its UPDATE.
detection_check: scraper/tests/integration/admin-write-database-clock.integration.test.ts fakes the app clock 5 min behind and ahead of the database and asserts every admin-save stamp lies between the database's now() before and after the save, that item 9 suggests only the post-save document, and that field_sources.updated_at never runs backwards across INSERT then UPDATE. It guards the named write paths only; a NEW write path that stamps new Date() into a column compared with a database time is not caught by any standing check.
